title: Pacific climate-mode indices explain the recent warming but not the 2006-2017 freshening that made the western North Pacific sigma0 26.5 outcrop region lighter (WOD ship and Argo casts, 1950-2025)
abstract: Question: is the freshening and lightening of the late-winter surface in the western North Pacific outcrop region of sigma0 26.5 (38-48 N, 150-170 E) a response to the Pacific climate modes, or a change that they do not explain? Approach: from 95,223 World Ocean Database ship and Argo casts (January-April, 30-50 N, 140 E-150 W, 1950-2025) we made annual 0-30 m and mixed-layer anomaly series with cell-month and year fixed effects and a cruise bootstrap. A pre-registered test fitted PDO, NPGO and North Pacific Index (Aleutian Low) predictors with lags of 0-5 yr on 1950-1995 and predicted 1996-2025. Results: the outcrop-box surface became lighter in a step near 2007 (sigma0 -0.108 kg/m3 in 2006-2017, -0.128 in 2018-2025, relative to 1965-1984; about 0 in 1985-2005). In 2006-2017 the cause was freshening (-0.13) at an unchanged temperature, not a front shift along the temperature-salinity line; in 2018-2025 it was warming (+0.86 deg C) at an unchanged salinity. The mode model predicted the warming (+0.33 of +0.36 deg C) but no freshening (+0.02 against -0.075) and 6% of the density change; this result held in two other boxes and in all sensitivity runs. Fitted on all years, the modes gave 20% of the density change. The subarctic box to the north also freshened; the subtropical box did not; local GPCP precipitation fell. Argo is not fresher than ships at crossovers. In 11 CMIP6 models the forced salinity change is +0.05 (internal SD 0.04); the observed -0.085 gives z = -2.7. At 160-170 E, within-type O2 on sigma0 26.5 follows the non-mode part of the surface density (r2 0.51), but half of its loss came before the 2007 surface step. Limitations: sparse winter ship data before 2000 and almost none in 1994-1999; linear index responses only; evaporation and salt transport not examined; one CMIP6 member per model; the O2 link is exploratory.
